[LINT.7.2] **An interval is valid only when `start <= end`** under its element
type's `<=` ([LINT.1.1]). Every other interval is **invalid**: one whose
`end < start`, and one with a NaN endpoint, for which `start <= end` is false
([LEXP.4.2]). A `null` endpoint does not make an interval invalid.

When the engine evaluates `start .. end` and the endpoints are two values, neither
`null`, that are not `start <= end`, it **must** raise a `ComputationError` of
kind `DOMAIN` ([LERR.1.4.10]). The fault is the `..` operation's own, so every
operation on the interval — `in`, `contains`, `overlaps`, `==`, `!=` and a
component read ([LINT.3] to [LINT.6]) — yields it whatever its other operand is,
`null` included ([LNUL.4.10]), and the engine handles it as it handles every
`ComputationError` ([LERR.1.4.7]). A `let` bound to an interval is evaluated
where it is used ([LLET.10.3]), so an invalid interval that no operation uses
raises nothing.
